result.title: What Places an Action Boundary? Structure-Aware Attribution for Temporal Action Localization
result.summary: Temporal action localization (TAL) detectors must identify actions and estimate their temporal boundaries, but localization remains a major source of detection errors. While understanding what determines boundary placement requires faithful attribution of temporal evidence, existing attribution methods have not sufficiently addressed the temporal structure of TAL or the need to tailor attribution to boundary localization. We introduce a structure-aware attribution framework that averages contributions across random evidence-restoration orders following the Shapley-Shubik principle. We make it tractable by using the detector's receptive field to limit which time steps are ordered individually, and by approximating each order with a soft gradient path. For boundary predictions, we further introduce cell-structured restoration orders and boundary-anchored references that selectively remove adjacent evidence. We also adapt faithfulness evaluation to assess the joint effects of contiguous temporal evidence and the direction of boundary displacement. Experiments on THUMOS14 and EPIC-KITCHENS-100 with TriDet and ActionFormer demonstrate improved attribution faithfulness over existing methods. Attribution analysis and controlled interventions further reveal that class-score changes do not reliably track boundary displacement, providing input-level evidence that classification relies on content less informative about boundary placement. Code and evaluation artifacts will be publicly released.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出结构感知归因框架，按 Shapley-Shubik 原则在随机证据恢复顺序上平均贡献，并以感受野与软梯度路径降低计算量，用于分析时序动作定位中边界由哪些连续证据决定。
AI.relevance_reason: 其对连续时序证据的归因与忠实性评价（含边界位移方向）可能为 latent 推理中的贡献分配、视觉证据筛选及停止/边界判断提供可核查的度量线索，但领域与 VLM 推理相距较远。
